rationale: 5 blocking patch findings confirmed in source across 3 files: NaN bypass in the service guard (critical, data corruption), CREATE/UPDATE HTTP status asymmetry for pct<0 and pct>100, OpenAPI minimum:0 contract dropped from the update schema, and a test gap leaving the NaN path undetected. No spec/story was present so acceptance was not run (compact profile, genuine no-spec). 0 deferred, 0 dismissed.

findings.title: CREATE path still returns 422 for negative pct
findings.problem: CategoryBudgetSpec.pct retains ge=0,le=100 (Pydantic), so POST /v1/admin/project-budget-groups returns 422 for a negative pct while PUT returns 400 for the same violation.
findings.impact: Clients receive different HTTP status codes for identical invalid input depending on the verb, breaking the uniform error contract introduced by this change.
findings.recommendation: Remove ge=0 from CategoryBudgetSpec.pct and extend the spec.pct < 0 (and isfinite) guard in _validate_group_categories to cover the create path as well.

findings.title: OpenAPI minimum:0 contract dropped from update pct field
findings.problem: ge=0 was removed from CategoryBudgetSpecUpdate.pct to move validation to the service layer, but no json_schema_extra was added to restore the minimum:0 annotation; le=100 (which provides maximum:100) was kept, making the schema asymmetric.
findings.impact: The OpenAPI spec no longer advertises a lower bound on pct for the update endpoint; generated SDKs, docs, and contract tests lose the minimum:0 assertion.
findings.recommendation: Add Field(le=100, json_schema_extra={'minimum': 0}, description='...') to CategoryBudgetSpecUpdate.pct to restore the schema annotation without reintroducing a Pydantic validation constraint.

findings.title: UPDATE pct>100 still returns 422 via Pydantic le=100
findings.problem: CategoryBudgetSpecUpdate.pct still carries le=100; submitting pct>100 on PUT returns 422 from Pydantic, while pct<0 returns 400 from the service guard. Symmetric range violations on the same field return different status codes.
findings.impact: Clients that switch from checking 422 to 400 for validation errors on this endpoint will silently miss the over-100 case.
findings.recommendation: Remove le=100 from CategoryBudgetSpecUpdate.pct and add a service-level guard for spec.pct > 100 in _validate_group_categories alongside the existing pct < 0 check.

findings.title: NaN pct bypasses guard and corrupts budget total
findings.problem: The guard checks spec.pct < 0; float('nan') < 0 is False in Python, so NaN passes. Before this change, ge=0 on the Pydantic field rejected NaN (nan >= 0 evaluates False → Pydantic raises 422). Removing ge=0 without adding math.isfinite opened a NaN code path to the database.
findings.impact: sum() of category pcts becomes NaN; abs(NaN - 100.0) > PCT_SUM_TOLERANCE evaluates to False so the 100% check also passes; NaN is written as max_budget to the database, silently corrupting the budget group.
findings.recommendation: Replace the guard with: if not math.isfinite(spec.pct) or spec.pct < 0 — this rejects NaN, -inf, and negative values in one expression. Import math at the top of the file if not already present.

findings.title: test_system_rejects_invalid_distribution_values covers only negative case
findings.problem: test_system_rejects_invalid_distribution_values has a single parametrize case ('negative', pct=-10); NaN and boundary pct=-0.001 are absent.
findings.impact: The NaN bypass opened by removing ge=0 (CR-004) is undetectable by the test suite; future regressions on this guard go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add parametrize cases for pct=float('nan') and pct=-0.001; assert ExtendedHTTPException with code=400 and that the message contains the offending category key.
